answer.evidence: The grey header band (rows 1-4) brightens from #8d9095 to #f3f4f7, so row 4 is the lightest row and works as a front-edge line. It is followed by two dark eave-shadow rows (5-6), and below that comes the dark front face with the four screens (rows 7-21) and base (22-23). The band is a gradient and could also be read as a front-facing marquee strip, so it is borderline. It meets the edge-line plus shadow pattern of evidence (a), so I count it as a 4-row top. The front face is about 19 rows tall. No receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are near the references: 15 visible tones per tile against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the well, 13% near-flat coverage (same as the stall), and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline leans navy rather than pure black. By eye the piece is shallower than those references. The large dark body panel and the white top band are close to flat, with only about 2-3 lightness steps each and no grain, speckle or per-element shading. The detail sits only in four small screens and three-tone red stools. The cheese stall and the well have 5-6 steps per material (shaded tiles, wood grain, stone by stone). The candidate reads more like a clean graphic sticker than a Beodeul-grade prop.
